title: What If a Tornado Was 2.6 Miles Wide? One Was

scenes.text: What if a tornado was wider than a small town? In 2013, one was.
On May 31, 2013, near El Reno, Oklahoma, a tornado grew to 2.6 miles wide. The widest ever measured.
Radar clocked winds near 300 miles an hour inside small spinning vortices within it.
It sped up from about 20 to 55 miles an hour in minutes. Some vortices moved over 100.
It stayed on the ground for 40 minutes and covered about 16 miles.
Its official rating is only EF3. Ratings come from damage, and its strongest winds hit almost nothing.
